scope.summary: Implement a `PinConstraint` (per-particle positional lock, inv_mass = 0) and a `FreezeRegion` operator/model command that pins a named set of particles for the duration of a simulation run or until explicitly unpinned, mirroring MD's Pin and Freeze interactive tools
acceptance_criteria: `GarmentSpec` gains `pin_regions: Vec<PinRegionSpec>` where `PinRegionSpec` carries `panel_id: String`, `vertex_selector: PinSelector` (enum: `BoundaryAll`, `VertexIds(Vec<u32>)`, `UvRegion { u_min, u_max, v_min, v_max }`), and `unpin_at_frame: Option<u32>`

At `SolverMesh` build time, pinned vertices receive `GpuParticle.inv_mass = 0.0`; the WGSL `integrate.wgsl` shader skips force integration for particles with `inv_mass == 0.0` (already defined in the spec struct comment at line 1474)

When `unpin_at_frame` is set, the animation loop (MT-289) uploads an updated particle buffer at that frame restoring the original `inv_mass` from the fabric density; the event `TailorPinRegionReleased` is emitted to the EventLedger

An MCP tool `pin_region` is exposed (parallel to `place_trim`) accepting `garment_id`, `panel_id`, and `vertex_selector`; models can pin a garment shoulder panel, run simulation, and observe the rest of the garment draping while the pinned region is held
Integration test: pin the waistband of a skirt, run a drape sim, assert pinned vertices have displacement < 0.1 mm and the rest of the skirt drapes normally (NO_INTERPENETRATION passes)

All operator-facing scope is implemented in src/frontend/handshake_native with native wgpu/egui, AccessKit author_id, Argus inspection/steering/capture, and no Tailor React, Tauri-command, WebView, data-testid-only, or rendered-PNG frontend path.

The exact TailorSurfaceDescriptor row MT-336 enumerates every route, pane, control author_id, dynamic entity-key rule, action, state, help anchor, permission, undo policy, receipt, and command binding; wildcard-only evidence is rejected.

Applicable blank, loading, populated, stale/conflict, cancelled, failed, retry, permission, keyboard/focus, narrow/4K/DPI, overlap/clipping, and no-focus-steal states are covered by the registry-derived Argus matrix.
scope.risk_if_missed: Operators and models cannot hold garment regions in place during interactive draping or animation; MD-style fitting workflows (hold collar while draping bodice, freeze pinned hem while re-simming below) are impossible. The refit pipeline (MT-299-MT-316) also lacks a pin-assist for stable garment transfer.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.

Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

required_changes_before_execution: Bind the CPU reference and interactive XPBD methods to the authoritative schedule, material coupons, strain limits, and failure checks.
MT-336 owns the pin/freeze primitive; MT-420 owns animation and native-UI integration and depends on MT-336.
Replace legacy app/src or app/src-tauri targets with the native Handshake shell and native Tailor paths.
Added gui_obligation, user_manual_obligation, and HBR-INT-009 tier obligations from the current MT template without removing original scope.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.
Use PostgreSQL RLS/FORCE RLS and ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; UI filtering is never the security boundary.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
